class_removed: Guards that test a proxy for the property the consumer needs. docs/standards/launch_ready_guards.md proposes five, each with a failing case reproduced against the live repo and pod: READY must consume the contract it already prints (a mix summing to 1.69013 prints FAIL and READY on adjacent lines and exits 0, reproduced); the token cache must be keyed on tokenizer behaviour, not just its vocabulary (three edits to the real tokenizer keep vfp 0bce3584bc24f255 while changing the token stream, reproduced on the pod); pod drift must cover the launcher and the tokenizer (data/tokenizer.json is named in pod_drift.SCOPE and has zero manifest entries because it is gitignored); the environment must be compared to the verified one before launch, not only on resume; the resolved flags must be the effective values.

corrections: Two claims I had to withdraw while writing this. (1) I believed I had edited train.py during the stage-1 startup gate. The edits are 029c43a at 19:48:58; the launch is d86bfc2 at 20:42:50, 54 minutes later, and the train.py blob has not changed since 19:48. Nothing was edited during the gate. The gap is still real and worth naming: nothing in the repo would have stopped it. pre-commit reads no running-run state, check_pod_drift SKIPs on a dev checkout, and the freeze lives in fb's order and a sentence in this file. (2) I had written that the eval scripts store gen[-300:], repeating the comment rather than checking; three of five store the full text and two did not. (3) I told fb the 3.24B milestone was ~1.5 h out; it is 22:36, four minutes off fb's independent estimate. (4) I proposed retracting the 6.6% and 25.4% base-code figures on fb's order and then found the premise was false: degeneration_rate applies [-300:] itself, so a tail-only artifact is idempotent for that metric and five of six figures recompute exactly. The sixth, L1 3-shot, is genuinely gone and is retracted as be.l1_3shot_retracted. Checking the premise before executing is what found the real defect; executing the order as given would have voided three good numbers and missed the broken one.

class_removed: Guards that test a proxy for the property the consumer needs. docs/standards/launch_ready_guards.md proposes five, each with a failing case reproduced against the live repo and pod: READY must consume the contract it already prints (a mix summing to 1.69013 prints FAIL and READY on adjacent lines and exits 0, reproduced); the token cache must be keyed on tokenizer behaviour, not just its vocabulary (three edits to the real tokenizer keep vfp 0bce3584bc24f255 while changing the token stream, reproduced on the pod); pod drift must cover the launcher and the tokenizer (data/tokenizer.json is named in pod_drift.SCOPE and has zero manifest entries because it is gitignored); the environment must be compared to the verified one before launch, not only on resume; the resolved flags must be the effective values.
landed_now: readout_30b param_line: params printed for both sides of a readout, computed from the checkpoint rather than stamped, with aliasing keyed on (data_ptr, numel). selftest 2b builds a tied and an untied checkpoint and asserts they render differently -- the failing case is that a value-equality key calls the untied one tied and hides a doubled embedding table. Verified against the pod: ckpt_p324.pt reads 206.1M (tied head; state_dict 239.7M).
differently: Check that commanded values are effective values before calling a launch ready; a flag string is a request, and only the log or the checkpoint says what happened. Cite symbols rather than line numbers when another session owns the file. Never write to the shared checkout when a worktree can do the job.
note: runs/retro.jsonl line 3 is pretty-printed across ten physical lines (3b's row). It is valid JSON and it breaks the one-object-per-line reader every other consumer uses; a naive `for line in f: json.loads(line)` raises on line 2 of it. Not my row to rewrite -- flagged for 3b or de.
